title: Where the logs live
briefing: Every Linux system follows the same map:
/var   data that varies: caches, mail, spools... and logs
expert_briefing: Logs tell you what the machine did while you weren't looking.
tips: `cd DIRECTORY` moves you. Watch your prompt change as you travel.
objective: Move into the directory where the system keeps its log files, and list what's inside.
expert_objective: Go where the logs live. Look around.
hints: Logs are data that *varies* over time. Which top-level directory on the map is for that? Logs live one level below it.
The logs are in /var/log. `cd` changes directory.

reactions.say: Close — you're in /var. One of the directories in here holds the logs. List it.
Not every door opens for you. Remember who you are (whoami). We'll come back to permissions.

explanation: `cd /var/log` uses an absolute path. From /var, `cd log` (relative) gets you there too; `cd ..` climbs one level; a bare `cd` always takes you home and `cd -` goes back. You'll spend a lot of your life in /var/log.
